teaser.text: Illumina, Inc. sells the equipment and supplies laboratories use to read genetic material and turn it into data. Its business is built around a simple cycle: place an instrument, sell the materials and software that keep it working, and collect payment from laboratories whose research or testing creates the demand.

blocks.heading: Where could Illumina's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $167.64 in October 2027, a 36% loss. It is $189.30 in October 2029, a 28% loss. The bear case has 27% probability; the base case has 53%. The bull case has 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Illumina?

paragraphs.text: The base revenue path is $4,980 million at a 17.3% normalized net margin. Revenue then reaches $5,330 million at a 17.7% margin, before ending at $5,700 million and an 18.0% margin. Clinical consumables outside Greater China grew 15% in Q2 2026, and about 70% of NovaSeq X placements were clinical. Management also guided to 2026 revenue of $4.60–$4.64 billion and a 23.4%–23.6% operating margin, while retaining a high-single-digit 2027 growth ambition.

The bear case gives $628 million on $4,650 million of revenue in 2027. Its normalized net margin is 13.5%. Earnings then fall to $598 million and $605 million, as research weakness, China uncertainty and pricing pressure prevent recovery. Research and applied consumables outside Greater China fell 7%, while Greater China revenue declined 12% in Q2 2026. More than 30% data growth produced only 8% consumables growth in a prior quarter, showing the monetization risk.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Illumina really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation deserves a separate deduction. Illumina added back $275 million of share-based compensation in 2025 because no cash left at the grant date. Shareholders nevertheless bear dilution unless the company later spends cash to offset it. The memo’s “real free cash flow” subtracts that ownership cost once.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Illumina today?

paragraphs.text: Today’s 49.1x trailing P/E means investors pay $49.10 for each dollar of recent earnings. That is demanding because those earnings must become larger and durable enough to justify the price.

blocks.heading: What has Illumina guided for FY2026?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast points to a lower share price unless Illumina turns clinical demand and instrument placements into durable earnings growth. Management guides FY2026 revenue to $4.60–$4.64 billion. It guides to a non-GAAP operating margin of 23.4%–23.6% and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $5.30–$5.40. Its high-single-digit revenue-growth ambition for 2027 depends on clinical demand, placements converting to consumables, and new products adding growth.

Clinical consumables growth must offset weak research demand, and NovaSeq X placements must become regular purchases. Management says clinical customers need six to nine months to reach normal consumables purchasing. Q3 results on October 29, 2026 will test 4.5% rest-of-world organic growth and 150 basis points of sequential operating-margin expansion. The October 30, 2026 securities-litigation hearing updates the GRAIL-related legal overhang. The November 2, 2026 Delaware hearing updates it again.

blocks.heading: Did Illumina keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The 2025 operating result partly fulfilled management’s promises. In February 2025, management promised an adjusted operating margin of approximately 23% for the year. It forecast adjusted earnings per share of $4.50–$4.65 and delivered $4.84. It delivered a 23.1% adjusted margin, but annual revenue was essentially flat, with stronger growth outside China.

blocks.heading: What have Illumina's revenue and profit done?

paragraphs.text: Illumina’s sales are recovering, but clinical laboratories are carrying the recovery.
Illumina’s ordinary operating profitability improved in 2025, although unusual gains made the reported comparison look worse.
